# <span id="aanchor330"></span> Heating Value Uncertainty Details

BLM regulations prescribe that heating value uncertainty must be within +/- 2% for a high volume FMP and within +/- 1% for a very high volume FMP. FLOWCAL performs this calculation for BLM properties as part of the source apply process and generates an exception if the uncertainty is not within range. If the calculation is unsuccessful, an error exception will be written. (See: [Exceptions 9021 - 9024](../Exceptions/Exception%20Directory/9000/9000-9999.md))

The FMP calculation process is as follows:

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">N</span> = The total number of values being used in calculation

2.  Calculate the heating value variability.
    <div>

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 210;height: 41;" />

    Where:

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">V<sub>(95%)</sub></span> = Heating value variance, 95% confidence interval

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">σHV</span> = Standard deviation of previous five samples

    <span style="font-family: Cambria;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;text-decoration: overline;">HV</span> = Average heating value, *μ*

    <span style="font-family: Cambria;font-style: italic;font-weight: bold;text-decoration: none;">2.776</span> = Student t-distribution for a probability of 0.05 and 4 degrees of freedom

    Example (continued):

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">V<sub>(95%)</sub></span><span style="font-family: Cambria;">= 100 \* 1.53708 \* 2.776 / 1160.85 = <u>0.367572%</u></span>

    </div>
3.  Calculate heating value uncertainty.
    <div>

    

<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 180;height: 58;" />

    Where:

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">U<sub>HV</sub></span> = Heating value uncertainty

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-style: italic; font-weight: bold;">N</span> = Number of samples taken per year as determined by FMP tier

    |     FMP Tier     | Samples Per Year (*N*) |
    |:----------------:|:----------------------:|
    | Very High Volume |           12           |
    |   High Volume    |           4            |
    |    Low Volume    |           2            |
    | Very Low Volume  |           1            |

     

    <div class="example">

    <a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler togglerBRDToggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCTogglerHotSpot_BRDToggler MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Example Cont">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Example (continued)</a>

    <div style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Example Cont">

    FMP Tier = Very High Volume (<span style="font-family: Cambria; font-style: italic;">N = 12</span>)

    <span style="font-family: Cambria; font-weight: bold; font-style: italic;">U<sub>HV</sub></span> = 0.951 \* 0.367572 \* <span style="font-family: 'Symbol'">Ö</span>( 1/12 ) = <u>0.100909%</u>

    For a very high volume meter, as used in this example, the heating value uncertainty must be less than 1%. Therefore, the final result of 0.100909% is within tolerance and no exception will be written.
